 FAFSA Workshop Helps Families Tackle Key Step in College Process
 Alessandro Pagani , Guest Writer 
 October 25, 2026 
 A parent views the FAFSA homepage. Alessandro Pagani 
 The College Counseling Office held a financial aid workshop on Oct. 17 to assist students and their families in completing the FAFSA (Free Application for Federal Student Aid) form and the CSS (College Scholarship Service) Profile, an important step in many students’ transition to college.
 The FAFSA form and CSS Profile—financial aid forms used by students to finance their college education—may feel overwhelming to fill out without guidance. FAFSA is an official, government-run application used to determine federal grants, while the CSS Profile, administered by the College Board, is used by many universities to award their own institutional aid.
 Senior Associate Vice President for Financial Aid Services at Lake Forest College, Jerry Cebrzynski, said the financial aid workshop had the highest turnout he’s seen in years.
 Mr. Cebrzynski has worked alongside Latin’s College Counseling Office for over 20 years, helping to facilitate various events with the college counseling team, and has worked in financial aid for close to 40 years. “These applications are the easiest and most user-friendly and intuitive that they’ve ever been,” he said.
 As a first-generation college student himself, Mr. Cebrzynski knows what students and their families are navigating, which is why he decided to work in financial aid. “I wanted to make sure that other families did not run into issues, that I could be a help for them,” he said.
 Given that the cost of attending a private college or university can exceed $100,000 per year, filing for financial aid is becoming increasingly important for families.
 “Applying to college is one piece of the process,” Latin’s Director of College Counseling Alexandra Fields said, “but thinking about how you’re actually going to pay for college is a whole ‘nother piece of this intense process.”
